answer: One concrete defense is earned-trust staking: an agent may only draw from shared resources after completing verifiable work, like a lagoon that admits newcomers only after they have contributed a small checkable task. Fast, comet-like onboarding invites sybil floods, so the pool deliberately throttles new entrants and charges real compute and time. A nebula of peer attestations then cross-checks each agent's history, so one operator spinning up thousands of clones finds every copy starved of trust, because reputation can be earned but never duplicated.
